sections.html:
Bowie is a city in Prince George's County and its largest municipality. It is the fifth most populous city in Maryland and the third largest by area, at an elevation of about 154 feet.

Published area figures differ: Wikipedia lists 20.55 square miles in its infobox, 16 in the body text and cites a Census Bureau figure of 18.51. The 2020 census counted 58,329 residents, up from 50,269 in 2000, 54,727 in 2010 and 35,028 in 1970. The median age is 42.3, and the city has 20,991 households.

sections.h2: How did Bowie begin, and why does Levitt matter to sellers?
sections.html:
The city began as a railroad junction. In 1870 Ben Plumb sold lots where two lines met and called the settlement Huntington City. It was rechartered in 1880 as Bowie, named for Oden Bowie, a former governor and railroad president. Old Town Bowie is that original core.

The larger change came in 1957, when Levitt and Sons bought the Belair Estate and built the Belair community. Bowie annexed the Levitt land in 1959 and was re-incorporated as a city in 1963. Most residents today live in that Levitt-planned community built in the 1960s, and its street names follow alphabetical themes by section.

Because so many homes date to the same era, buyers can compare one house against its neighbors easily, and a seller should expect questions about what has been updated.

sections.h2: What historic places stand in Bowie?
sections.html:
Belair Mansion, built around 1745, is a Georgian house once owned by Governors Samuel Ogle and Benjamin Ogle, and it is on the National Register of Historic Places. The Belair Stud racing operation ran until 1957, and Belair Stable is now a museum.

Other listed sites include the Bowie Railroad Buildings, Sacred Heart Catholic Church and Melford. Owners near these sites should ask the city and county whether any historic-property rules apply before planning exterior work.

A 2007 estimate put median household income at $99,105. Per capita income ranks seventh in Prince George's County and 65th in Maryland. I-595 and US 50 link Bowie to both Washington and Annapolis.

sections.h2: What roads and transit serve Bowie?
sections.html:
I-595 and US 50, known here as the John Hanson Highway, run east to west through the city and connect Washington with Annapolis. US 301 and MD 3 run along the eastern edge toward Waldorf, La Plata and Baltimore.

  • MD 197, 214, 450 and 564 are the other state routes through town.
  • MARC's Penn Line serves the Bowie State station.
  • Bowie State University, north of the city, has operated since 1865.

sections.h2: Which schools and parks serve Bowie?
sections.html:
Public schools belong to Prince George's County Public Schools. Bowie High is the high school, and the middle schools are Benjamin Tasker and Samuel Ogle. Elementary schools include Heather Hills, Kenilworth, Northview, Pointer Ridge, Rockledge, Tulip Grove, Whitehall and Yorktown.

The city has about 2,000 acres of parkland and open space, including Allen Pond Park with its ice arena, plus Foxhill, Buckingham, Somerset, Whitemarsh and Jericho parks. It also has 72 ball fields, three community centers, the Bowie Town Center and the 800-seat Bowie Center for the Performing Arts. The Chesapeake Baysox, an Eastern League team, play at Prince George's Stadium.

sections.h2: Who governs Bowie, and which tax rates apply?
sections.html:
Bowie uses a council-manager form of government under its charter, with Michael Estève as mayor, according to Wikipedia. The city police department is the primary agency, backed by county police, park police and the Sheriff's Office.

A Bowie house is billed by both city and county. For fiscal 2026, the General Assembly's staff table lists $0.8760 per $100 for Bowie and $1.0000 for the county. The county says its rate is reduced for incorporated areas but the county page does not state the Bowie figure.

  • The state adds $0.1120 per $100.
  • M-NCPPC adds $0.2940 and the Washington Suburban Transit Commission $0.0260.
  • The county bill comes out in July, and full payment is due September 30.
  • A principal residence can pay half by September 30 and half by December 31.

For a sale, the settlement agent pays the bill out of proceeds, so what a seller needs is the payoff amount for the current year.

sections.h2: What if a Bowie house has unpaid taxes?
sections.html:
Real property taxes still unpaid by the second Monday in May are sold to the highest bidder at the county's annual tax sale. The county's Tax Facts guide gives the late charge as 1.67% per month, and there is no excuse for a missing bill.

Treasury Customer Service, 301-952-4030, is the number for a payoff. A seller who is behind may still close, provided the arrears are paid from the price.

Yes, through the city rather than the county. The county's rental page says Bowie is among the municipalities it does not license, and it tells owners to look up the property on the state's real property search: if the Town column shows Bowie, apply with Bowie.

If a former rental has a license problem or an unpermitted conversion, the owner may want to resolve it before a sale. County code compliance enforces its rules through a Notice of Violation or a Civil Citation. Ask the city which office handles code complaints for a property inside Bowie.

sections.h2: What do transfer taxes look like on a Bowie sale?
sections.html:
The county's transfer tax is 1.4% and its recordation tax is $2.75 per $500 of consideration, per a 2026 General Assembly staff table. The state adds a 0.5% transfer tax.

Who pays which share is decided in the contract. Title companies print the full figures on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What must a Bowie seller disclose?
sections.html: A seller of one to four units gives the buyer a state disclosure or disclaimer statement on or before contract signing under Maryland Real Property Code 10-702. The disclaimer says the house is sold as-is except for latent defects the seller knows about. Estates and trusts, bank-owned foreclosures and tax sales are exempt.

sections.h2: What payment options does the county offer Bowie owners?
sections.html:
Owners pay Prince George's County online, by phone, by mail or in person. Online fees are $1.50 for an e-check, $3.95 for a Visa debit card and 2.45% for other cards, and the phone line is 855-516-1830 with added fees.

  • Mail to P.O. Box 37050, New York, NY 10087, with the bill stub.
  • Counter at 1301 McCormick Drive, Suite 1100, Largo, open 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. weekdays, with no cash accepted.
  • A 24-hour walk-up slot takes checks, money orders and cashier's checks.

A Front Foot Benefit charge for sewer or water pipes in the street (WSSC, 301-206-8032) or a solid waste charge may also appear on the bill.

faqs.q: What is the Bowie, MD property tax rate?
faqs.a: The fiscal 2026 city rate is $0.8760 per $100, according to a General Assembly staff table. The county rate is $1.0000, reduced in incorporated areas, and the state rate is $0.1120.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Bowie?
faqs.a: Full payment to Prince George's County is due September 30. Principal residences can pay half by September 30 and half by December 31.

faqs.q: Does the county or the city license my Bowie rental?
faqs.a: The city does. Prince George's County says Bowie is on the list of municipalities it does not license.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay Bowie property taxes?
faqs.a: Taxes unpaid by the second Monday in May go to the county's annual tax sale. The Tax Facts guide lists the late charge at 1.67% per month.
Bowie High School, run by Prince George's County Public Schools. Middle schools include Benjamin Tasker and Samuel Ogle.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax in Bowie?
faqs.a: The county transfer tax is 1.4% and the state adds 0.5%. Recordation is $2.75 per $500. Confirm the exact split with the settlement agent.

faqs.q: Is Bowie in a flood or hail zone?
faqs.a: We could not confirm a flood or hail rating for Bowie on official pages, so check FEMA maps and ask your insurer.
